title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed into a predictable, high-impact event without adequate preparation for the traffic conditions that would result. Multiple vehicles became immobilized when their batteries depleted while trapped in severe congestion during Fourth of July celebrations near San Francisco. The failure occurred at the operational level: the system was used in conditions—extreme traffic volume and road closures—that exceeded its design assumptions, and there was no contingency for prolonged immobility.

This is a deployment problem, not a failure of the driving system itself. The vehicles operated as designed, but were sent into an environment where that design was insufficient. Catching this would have required scenario planning before the event: modeling battery drain under gridlock, establishing geofence exclusions around high-congestion areas on that date, or positioning vehicles with safety margins that account for traffic unpredictability.

One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though it is not established whether this resulted from the fire hazard itself or from the stressed conditions of the day. The broader failure shows the difference between a system that can drive autonomously and one that can operate safely within the full range of foreseeable urban conditions.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in severe traffic congestion. Video evidence showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets near the Golden Gate Bridge fireworks display. The company attributed the problem to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unexpected road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles, with some requiring towing. The company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its resilience during future traffic disruptions.

One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. A passenger experienced an autonomous vehicle continue driving when fireworks were set off nearby, while another witness spent nearly two hours in traffic before Waymo vehicles were cleared from the roadway. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated they will hold conversations with public and private partners to improve traffic management for similar events going forward, noting that over 100,000 people in the area experienced delays.
